protocol: per-gene z-score within each study, then either (a) Mahalanobis distance in 10 PCA components fitted on OSD-46, or (b) mean 1 - Pearson correlation to the 5 nearest OSD-46 arrays

preDeclaredExpectations.control1: duplicate must rank at or below the reference distribution
preDeclaredExpectations.control2: different platform must rank above it, AUC >= 0.9

control1_duplicate.why: OSD-320 holds the same arrays as OSD-46, so it should look like ordinary training data, not like a novelty

control2_platformShift.why: OSD-782 is a different measurement platform, so it should be flagged. Lower than 0.5 means the score calls a platform shift *more familiar* than the training data itself.
control2_platformShift.confound: platform, preparation protocol and organism part all move together with this study; per-gene standardisation is needed to compare across platforms and it deletes gene-level mean differences, which is much of what a platform shift is

control3_heldOutGroups.why: ordinary held-out groups must not be flagged, or the score fires on normal use

mechanism: cross-platform comparison requires per-gene standardisation, which removes gene-level mean shifts that are much of what a platform shift consists of

in-sample Mahalanobis distances are inflated by about sqrt((n-1)/(n-p)); with 44 arrays and 10 components that is 1.13x, larger than the gap between an ordinary and an unusual sample, so a new study looks nearer than the training data unless the reference is scored leave-one-out

the duplicate check also exposes scale sensitivity: a sample that is effectively in the training set is scored by a model fitted on all of it, while reference samples are scored with 43, and that difference alone moves the Mahalanobis AUC to 0.735

productConsequence.servedOodFlag: must not be presented as a validated novelty detector. It may describe distance from the training cloud; it must not say 'outside distribution' as if a threshold had been validated
productConsequence.intervalAdvice: conformal intervals with measured coverage remain the defensible uncertainty mechanism, with empirical and nominal coverage always shown separately

inStudyScoreQuantiles.note: descriptive quantiles of leave-one-out training-study scores. They are not thresholds; supplying one would be the claim this phase refutes.

uncertaintyCarriedOver.statement: empirical and nominal coverage stay distinct everywhere; no interval is described as a 90 % interval unless its measured coverage reached it
